title.narrative: Study on opportunities for leveraging SMEs in agribusiness

description.narrative: The overall purpose of this study is to outline the best approach and strategic steps for Dutch - Mozambican cooperation towards local economic development with focus on micro, small and medium enterprises (M)SMEs in the agro & food and horticulture sectors. The results of this project contribute to the analysis and systematization of the current situation of (M)SMEs and entrepreneurship by identifying key related constraints and barriers to start-up or scale-up their enterprises under a value chain approach. In addition to business-related challenges, the study will also include geographical or ethnic/cultural dynamics and barriers for youth, female and experienced entrepreneurs in rural and urban contexts. The study also provides an overview of the most relevant initiatives on entrepreneurship in agribusiness initiated by Mozambique, the Netherlands or other donors and determines concrete opportunities for bilateral cooperation, in particular where the Netherlands can provide an added value to enable sustainable local economic development. This will enable follow-up interventions in synergy or complementing already existing investments. Besides, the study will determine which provinces of the Zambezi valley offer most opportunities for agribusiness; which will enable to define the geographical focus of the embassy in line with the MACs 2023-2026.The project has a positive impact on:SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth;Target 8.3: Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovationSDG 2: Food security

Agribusiness Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) dominate the agricultural sector and they are crucial actors for sustainable socioeconomic development. The study tidentified the bottlenecks of these MSMEs and suggests 6 leveraging points to unlock their economic potential. Chapter two describes six themes that constrain agribusiness MSMEs from scaling up: (1) Access to finance, (2) Access to knowledge, (3) Access to markets, (4) (Downstream) Value addition, (5) Scale-up impact makers, and (6) Transport and logistics.
The findings of this study have led to specific recommendations for the Beira corridor and for Cabo Delgado (priority areas of the Netherlands in Mozambique. Priorities regarding value chains, target groups, and activities are offered as the Netherlands Embassy cannot focus on all identified bottlenecks.
I line with the above, the assignment idelivers also a value chain selection tool which enables the Dutch embassy in Maputo to select their ifuture nterventions in the field of agri-business to develop local economy by leveraging micro ans small scale enterprises. The criteria for slection of value chains are: (1) Production push, (2) Market pull, (3) Production potential, (4) Productivity, (5) Adding Value, (6) Internationalization, (7) NFS Impact, (8) Gender Inequality, (9) Job Creation, (10) Dutch policy and funds, and (11) Political will. Furthermore, each criterion is weighed to indicate the importance of that criteria, ultimately to provide a prioritized list of value chains. These ‘weights’ can be changed according to the priority of the Netherlands Embassy.

The study: a) provided up to date information for the ellaboration of the new Multi Anual Country Strategy (MACS _ 2023-2026 with focus on local private sector development targeting primarily the agri&food sector.
